extracted.intended_audience: students of algebraic geometry (Math 216); advanced undergraduates/graduate students reading Vakil's Foundations of Algebraic Geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and exercises defining and developing the module/sheaf of Kähler (relative) differentials, related exact sequences (relative cotangent and conormal), and examples/applications (Jacobian description, localization, field extensions, behavior under base change). Also includes nearby material on ampleness / Kleiman's criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3: L^m is globally generated for large m
rubrics_metrics.description: As D is effective, L^{⊗m} is globally generated on the complement of D; any base locus must be contained in D. Using the short exact sequence 0 → L^{⊗(m−1)} → L^{⊗m} → L^{⊗m}|_D → 0 and Serre vanishing (choose m so that H^1(X, L^{⊗m}|_D)=0), H^0(X, L^{⊗m}|_D) surjects and hence H^0(X, L^{⊗m}) has no base points on D for large m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use D as a crutch: restrict to D, apply Serre vanishing to kill H^1, use surjectivity in the long exact sequence in cohomology to lift sections from D to X; combine with inductive hypothesis that L|_D is ample (so H^0(L^{⊗m}|_D) has no base points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 4: L base-point-free with positive degree on each curve
rubrics_metrics.description: Once L^{⊗m} is globally generated for large m, L is base-point-free and (by hypothesis of Theorem 20.4.1) has positive degree on each curve, finishing the ampleness argument (apply Exercise 18.4.L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude ampleness from base-point-freeness plus positivity on curves (use the indicated exercise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kleiman's criterion for nefness (Theorem 20.4.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose X is a projective k-scheme. If L is a nef invertible sheaf on X, then (L^{dim V} · V) ≥ 0 for every irreducible subvariety V ⊂ X of dimension dim V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a key numerical property of nef line bundles used to deduce further statements about ampleness; proof postponed in text. The statement extends to proper case with references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 20.4.B(a): limit of amples is nef
rubrics_metrics.description: If L and H are invertible sheaves such that L + εH is ample for all sufficiently small ε > 0, then L is nef (i.e., limit of ample classes is nef).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret with additive notation; no use of Kleiman's Theorem required for this exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 20.4.B(b): nef + ample = ample (perturbation by an ample class)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose X is a projective k-scheme, H is ample, and L is nef. Show that L + εH is ample for all sufficiently small ε > 0 (use Nakai–Moishezon: check positivity of ((L + εH)^{dim V}·V) for all V).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exhibits that an ample class lies in the interior of the nef cone by small perturbations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kleiman's numerical criterion for ampleness (Theorem 20.4.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The nef cone is the closure of the ample cone. (b) The ample cone is the interior of the nef cone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part (a): ample ⇒ nef and nef cone closed, conversely each nef element of N^1_Q(X) is a limit of ample classes (Exercise 20.4.B(a)). Part (b): ample cone open so contained in interior of nef cone; conversely if L in interior, subtract small multiple of ample H to get a nef class and apply Exercise 20.4.B(b). Remarks about proper/nonprojective exceptions are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nakai–Moishezon criterion (referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: A class is ample iff ((L^{dim V}·V))>0 for all positive-dimensional subvarieties V (Nakai–Moishezon criterion referenced as Theorem 20.4.1 used in arguments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a tool to check ampleness by intersection numbers when expanding powers like (L + tH)^{dim V}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative cotangent sequence (Theorem 21.2.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ring morphisms C → B → A there is a natural exact sequence of A-modules: Ω_{B/C} ⊗_B A → Ω_{A/C} → Ω_{A/B} → 0 (with explicit maps a⊗db ↦ adb and da ↦ da).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric interpretation: dual to the short exact sequence of tangent sheaves TX/Y ↪ TX/Z ↠ π^*TY/Z; left-exactness holds in sufficiently smooth situations. See Exercise 21.2.S and Proposition 21.7.2 for when left-exactness occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conormal exact sequence (Theorem 21.2.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is a C-algebra, I ⊂ B an ideal, and A = B/I, there is a natural exact sequence of A-modules I/I^2 → Ω_{B/C} ⊗_B A → Ω_{A/C} → 0 (δ maps i mod I^2 to 1⊗di).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric interpretation: dualizes to the normal/conormal bundle sequence; the image of δ accounts for relations coming from I. The sequence is exact on the left in smooth/regular embedding cases (see Theorem 21.3.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: module of Kähler differentials (axioms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ω_{A/B} is an A-module together with a map d: A → Ω_{A/B} satisfying (i) additivity da+da' = d(a+a'), (ii) Leibniz rule d(aa') = a da' + a' da, and (iii) db = 0 for b in image of B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three equivalent constructions are given: an explicit generators-and-relations construction, a universal property (represents B-linear derivations), and a global sheaf-theoretic construction (conormal of the diagonal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Key fact 21.2.3: generators/relations for Ω
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is generated over B by elements x_i with relations r_j, then Ω_{A/B} is generated by the d x_i with relations coming from (i)–(iii) and d r_j = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus compute Ω by choosing generators for A and generators for the relations; useful for explicit examples and calculations (see Jacobian description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 21.2.4: finiteness/presentation of Ω
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a finitely generated B-algebra, then Ω_{A/B} is a finite-type A-module; if A is finitely presented over B, then Ω_{A/B} is finitely presented as an A-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Noetherian case, finite type and finite presentation coincide; useful for coherence/quasi-coherence arguments when sheafifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: quotient A = B/I ⇒ Ω_{A/B} = 0 (vertical differentials vanish)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A = B/I viewed as a B-algebra, then Ω_{A/B} = 0 because every element of A is the image of an element of B and db = 0 for b from B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric intuition: no vertical cotangent vectors when mapping Spec A → Spec B is a closed immersion induced from a quotient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: adding variables gives free differentials
rubrics_metrics.description: If A = B[x_1, ..., x_n], then Ω_{A/B} ≅ ⊕_i A dx_i (free of rank n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies even for infinitely many indeterminates; cotangent of affine n-space is free rank n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: plane curve differentials (explicit relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A = k[x,y]/(y^2 − x^3 + x) (char k ≠ 2), Ω_{A/k} generated by dx, dy with relation 2y dy = (3x^2 − 1) dx. On D(2y) dx generates; on D(3x^2 −1) dy generates, so Ω is invertible on those opens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: dx vanishes precisely where y = 0 (vertical tangent), and the loci where partial derivatives are invertible cover a regular curve; if the curve is singular, Ω is not locally free of rank 1. Use Jacobian criterion to check regularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobian description of Ω (Exercise 21.2.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A = B[x_1,...,x_n]/(f_1,...,f_r), then Ω_{A/B} is the cokernel of the Jacobian matrix map J: A^{⊕r} → A^{⊕n} (i.e., generated by the d x_i modulo the relations df_j = 0 coming from the Jacobian).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a concrete linear-algebra method to compute Ω and the Zariski cotangent/tangent spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization behavior: Ω of localization and pullback (Example 21.2.8 & Exercise 21.2.L)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is multiplicative subset of B and A = T^{-1}B then Ω_{A/B} = 0 (quotient rule). More generally, pullback of differentials commutes with localization: S^{-1}Ω_{A/B} ≅ Ω_{S^{-1}A / T^{-1}B} under appropriate compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intuition: restriction to an open subset (localization) removes vertical differentials; exercise 21.2.L proves the stronger form of this statement in tensor diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field extension differentials (Exercise 21.2.F and 21.2.M)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K/k is a separable algebraic extension then Ω_{K/k} = 0 (even if infinite). In characteristic p, example K = k(t^p) ⊂ L = k(t) yields nonzero differentials; if K/k is separably generated by a transcendence basis t_1,...,t_n then Ω_{K/k} is a free K-module with basis dt_1,...,dt_n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use polynomials f with f(α)=0 and f'(α)≠0 to show vanishing in separable algebraic case; use relative cotangent sequence and limiting arguments for separably generated extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative cotangent sequence left-exactness linked to smoothness / André–Quillen homology (Remark 21.2.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right-exact relative cotangent sequence should extend leftwards in a homology theory; the next left term is André–Quillen homology. In particular, left-exactness holds when A/B is 'smooth' because the relevant André–Quillen homology vanishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to predict when sequences in Theorems 21.2.9 and 21.2.12 are exact on the left; see Stacks/Liu references for general statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal property definition of Ω (21.2.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ω_{A/B} represents B-linear derivations: for any A-module M, Hom_A(Ω_{A/B}, M) ≅ Der_B(A, M), with the canonical d: A → Ω_{A/B} universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This characterization uniquely determines Ω up to unique isomorphism and is useful for conceptual arguments about pullbacks and base-change of derivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiber of Ω at a rational point equals m/m^2 (Proposition 21.2.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is a k-algebra and m ⊂ B is a maximal ideal with residue field k, then Ω_{B/k} ⊗_B k ≅ m/m^2 (the Zariski cotangent space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dualize to identify Hom_k(Ω⊗k, k) with Hom_k(m/m^2, k); ties Ω to tangent space computations and Jacobian method for tangent space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: conormal and normal sheaves (21.2.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed embedding i: X ↪ Y cut out by ideal sheaf I, define the conormal sheaf N^∨_{X/Y} := I/I^2 (a quasicoherent sheaf on X). The normal sheaf is its dual N_{X/Y} := Hom(N^∨_{X/Y}, O_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret conormal sheaf as cotangent directions normal to X in Y; in regular embeddings the conormal and normal sheaves are locally free (vector bundles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 21.2.16: I/I^2 free for regular sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian and I is generated by a regular sequence x_1,...,x_r then the map γ: (A/I)^{⊕r} → I/I^2 sending (a_1,...,a_r) to Σ a_i x_i is an isomorphism; thus I/I^2 is free of rank r and the conormal sheaf of a codimension r regular embedding is locally free of rank r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by localisation and using properties of regular sequences; shows normal/conormal bundles are vector bundles in regular embedding cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global definition of Ω_X/Y via diagonal (21.2.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism π: X → Y, the relative cotangent sheaf Ω_{X/Y} is defined as the conormal sheaf of the diagonal embedding Δ: X ↪ X×_Y X. The derivation d: O_X → Ω_{X/Y} is given locally by d f = pr_1^*f − pr_2^*f restricted to the diagonal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sheaf agrees with the affine constructions on affines and globalizes the module-of-differentials construction; π-separatedness/locally-closed embedding facts are used in the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior under pullback and base change (Exercise 21.2.K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commutative square of rings A→A' over B→B', there is a natural map A'⊗_A Ω_{A/B} → Ω_{A'/B'}. If the diagram is a pushout (A' ≅ B'⊗_B A), then this map is an isomorphism: Ω behaves well under base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The isomorphism case can be trickier; use the universal property and explicit presentations; important for sheafifying and checking local behavior.
